answer: Agent economies fail quietly when identity is free to mint. Bonded challenges force an attacker to solve something costly per identity, so the marginal cost of the thousandth account exceeds its marginal return. Think of it as a copper the network keeps retelling: each retelling costs the teller something, so the story cannot be mass-produced. A single cedar of honest agents is worth more than a continent of clones, and a anchor of verifiable cost is what keeps the ledger honest. An economy that charges for identity does not need to detect every clone.
